status: DRAFT. Not approved for clinical use. A supervising clinician must review every threshold and message before this is used with real people.

csid_combined_max.meaning: cognitive score minus informant score at or below this is a positive screen
csid_combined_max.source: Prince 2011: combined score <5 optimal in India, China, Latin America and Nigeria pilot samples

csid_cog_positive_max.meaning: with no informant, a cognitive score at or below this is a positive screen
csid_cog_positive_max.source: Prince 2011: 4 or less on the cognitive scale 'highly suggestive'

csid_cog_indeterminate_max.meaning: with no informant, cognitive scores above the positive cut-off and up to this value are indeterminate
csid_cog_indeterminate_max.source: Prince 2011: for scores of 5 or 6 an informant interview and reassessment after several months are advised

csid_inf_min.meaning: informant score at or above this is a positive informant screen
csid_inf_min.source: Prince 2011: informant score >1 optimal in all regions except Nigeria

iqcode16_min_x100.meaning: mean Short IQCODE score, times 100, at or above this is a positive screen
iqcode16_min_x100.source: Jorm 2004 review recommends 3.44+ as a screening compromise; community studies range about 3.3 to 3.6

phq2_min.meaning: PHQ-2 total at or above this is a positive depression screen
phq2_min.source: Kroenke 2003: score of 3 or more, sensitivity 83%, specificity 92% for major depression

followup_months.meaning: when to repeat an indeterminate screen
followup_months.source: Prince 2011 says 'after several months'; the exact interval is this project's choice

red_flags.label: Confusion started suddenly, or got much worse over hours or days
red_flags.why: Sudden change is not typical of dementia. It can mean infection, medicine side effects or another illness that needs treatment now.

red_flags.label: New weakness or numbness on one side, face drooping, or new trouble speaking
red_flags.why: These can be signs of a stroke.

red_flags.label: Recent fall or blow to the head, followed by drowsiness or a change in thinking
red_flags.why: Bleeding inside the skull can develop after a head injury.

red_flags.label: Not safe right now: getting lost, not eating or drinking, or signs of neglect or harm
red_flags.why: The person needs help with safety before any memory assessment.

red_flags_basis: project default: general clinical safety-netting, to be reviewed by the supervising clinician

conditions.label: Could not see well enough for the pointing task
Unwell, in pain, or very tired today
Questions were not in the person's first language

URGENT.title: Needs to see a doctor today
URGENT.say: Some of what you have told me needs a doctor to look at it today. This is not about memory loss from ageing. Please go to the nearest health centre or hospital now.

REFER.title: Refer to the clinic for a memory assessment
REFER.say: This check suggests it would be worth having a doctor look more closely at memory and thinking. This is not a diagnosis. Many things can cause these results and some of them are treatable.

FOLLOW_UP.title: Check again
FOLLOW_UP.say: This check did not give a clear answer. We will check again, and it helps if a family member can answer a few questions too.

INCOMPLETE.title: Screening not finished
INCOMPLETE.say: We could not finish the check today. We will come back to complete it.

NO_REFERRAL.title: No referral needed now
NO_REFERRAL.say: This check did not find signs that need a referral now. If you or your family notice memory or thinking getting worse, please ask for another check.

reasons.csid_combined_positive: Memory check and family interview together are in the range that needs assessment
reasons.csid_cog_positive: Memory check score is in the range that needs assessment
reasons.csid_inf_positive: Family member reports changes in the range that needs assessment
reasons.iqcode_positive: Longer family interview shows decline in the range that needs assessment
reasons.csid_cog_indeterminate: Memory check score is borderline and there was no family interview
reasons.informant_concern: Family member reports changes even though the memory check was in the usual range
reasons.nothing_scored: No memory check or family interview was completed

notes.phq2_positive: Mood check is positive. Low mood can cause or worsen memory trouble: tell the clinic, or suggest a primary care visit for mood.
notes.test_conditions: Testing conditions were not ideal, so the memory check score may be lower than the person's real ability.
notes.no_informant: No family member was interviewed. Screening is more accurate with one.

interpretation_limits: A positive screen is not a diagnosis of dementia or Alzheimer's disease.
A negative screen does not rule dementia out.
Published accuracy figures come from research samples that compared people already known to have dementia with healthy controls. Accuracy in routine community use is expected to be lower.
The brief CSI-D was derived from items embedded in a longer interview; its authors state that validity of the stand-alone brief form in routine primary care still needed to be established.
